company_native: Technische Universität München, Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence
target_applications: eldercare assistance, tactile telemedicine (ECG/BP/ultrasound), rehabilitation, social interaction

base_type.value: wheeled mobile base (stable, low CoG) + extendable lifting column

actuators.value: torque-controlled 7-DoF arms (Franka Emika lineage), 1 ms control cycle, force sensing in all arm joints

end_effector.value: anthropomorphic artificial hand (demonstrated); telemedicine device handling (ultrasound probe)

sensors_head.value: cameras at eye level; expressive blinking eyes; chest touchscreen; microphones (speech interface)

sensors_wrist_hand.value: force/tactile sensors on arms; 3D cameras planned for arm coordination

software_stack.value: MIRMI stack; digital-twin collision pre-checking; ChatGPT natural-language command interface (15-20 commands, 2024); teleoperation for remote medical exams; no public SDK

safety_compliance.value: research, uncertified; Safety Motion Unit speed governor, 1 ms contact reaction, stop-on-touch

availability.value: not available; research prototypes; care-home deployment 'several years' away (TUM, May 2024)

deployment_evidence.value: model apartment trials at Geriatronics centre Garmisch-Partenkirchen with Caritas/LongLeif; telemedicine and rehab demos; ~90% grasp success on cups/glasses

notes: Company file also carries compact history of TUM's earlier wheeled dual-arm platforms TOMM (2017, two UR5 + full-body skin) and Rosie (~2009-2013, mecanum + two KUKA LWR-4, retired). Haddadin left MIRMI for MBZUAI Jan 2025 (verified); no GARMI spin-off company verifiable as of Aug 2026 despite discovery-note claim of spin-off intent.
